title: Local operational audit records and `ward audit`
description: Spec §9.4. Admission recorded before delivery, completion separately; sanitized fields only; bounded retention stated, not hidden.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T19: a pre-delivery audit persistence failure blocks delivery; a post-delivery failure is reported without claiming rollback
`ward audit --json` shows only current-project sanitized events and states its retention bound

implementationNotes:
WCLI-10/WCLI-11 SPLIT, RULED BY OPUM-AGENT (2026-09-29, ~05:32Z). Written here before WCLI-10 lands, at the ruling's own instruction, so this task's successor does not rebuild what WCLI-10 already carries.

WHAT WCLI-10 OWNS, and will already exist when this task starts. The run path: admission persisted before a credential is delivered, delivery, completion persisted after in its own transaction. The audit itself is a REQUIRED INJECTED PORT (src/application/transport.ts is the shape to copy; the port's record type is domain/vault-state.ts's AuditRecord), wired to a minimal vault-backed recorder writing into the vault's auditRecords collection via withAuditRecord. Admission re-reads the binding, the approval and the secret inside its own transaction, which is where revocation's admission-time semantics live. There is no field in AuditRecord a value could be written into, deliberately: no credential, no request or response body, no upstream message. auditHistoryLimit in domain/vault-state.ts is currently 500, oldest dropped first, global across projects rather than per project.

WHAT IS THIS TASK'S, and is not done by WCLI-10. (1) `ward audit --json`: current-project sanitized events only, and it STATES its retention bound rather than leaving a reader to discover it. (2) The retention bound's own statement and any change to it: WCLI-10 set a bound so the collection could not grow unbounded, but it is WCLI-11's to expose and to justify. (3) The fuller field set spec 9.4 names and WCLI-10 deliberately left unpopulated - observed OS identity, and the optional explicitly self-asserted actor/task labels. (4) T19, both halves: a pre-delivery audit persistence FAILURE blocks delivery, and a post-delivery failure is REPORTED WITHOUT CLAIMING ROLLBACK. The mechanism for both exists in WCLI-10 (the admission write throwing blocks the run; the completion write's failure is caught and surfaced as auditRecorded:false with exit 6 while the outcome still reports the operation honestly) - what is owed here is the evidence at the vault, not the plumbing.

THE REASONING, recorded so it is not re-litigated. A `ward run` that delivered a credential without an admission record would violate spec 9.4, and a no-op audit port in a shipped build would be the decorative control opum-sdlc explicitly forbids - a control that occupies the slot and stops anyone looking for a real one. The split is WCLI-10 owns the run path's control flow and the port; WCLI-11 owns the viewing command, the stated bound, the field set and T19.

EVIDENCE ALREADY IN PLACE from WCLI-10 that this task can build on rather than re-derive: test/run.test.ts asserts the ordering directly - a fake transport reads the vault at the moment it is called and must see the admission record and only the admission record; a failing admission is asserted to leave the transport uncalled and the history empty; a failing completion is asserted to leave the transport called exactly once, the admission record written, and the result carrying outcome succeeded with auditRecorded false and exit 6.
